newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BISHOP STRIKES TO HALT AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BISHOP STRIKES TO HALT AUSTRALIA.

text.p: West Indies fast bowler Ian Bishop removed openers Mark Taylor and Matthew Elliott in his first four overs to halt Australia's progress on the opening morning of the second test at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Friday.
Australia, who won the first test in Brisbane by 123 runs on Tuesday, were 73 for two at lunch after captain Taylor won the toss.
Bishop was overlooked by West Indies captain Courtney Walsh for new ball duties but revived the tourists' fortunes after Australia dominated the opening hour in fine conditions.
Taylor and Elliott looked poised to build a big opening partnership before Bishop struck with his second ball to remove Elliott for 29 with the total on 54.
Elliott, who struck five boundaries during his 78-minute stay at the crease, edged a full-length delivery outside his off stump to Brian Lara at first slip.

Although the ball came to Lara at a comfortable height, the West Indies vice-captain did well to hold the catch after wicketkeeper Courtney Browne dived across his line of vision in a failed attempt to take the chance.
Six overs later, Taylor drove another full-length delivery to Shivnarine Chanderpaul at short cover to fall for 27.
Australia number three Ricky Ponting was nine not out at the interval alongside Mark Waugh on four.
Fast bowler Jason Gillespie made his test debut for the home side after paceman Paul Reiffel was ruled out before start of play with a neck muscle strain.
West Indies named an unchanged side after fast bowler Kenneth Benjamin passed a fitness test on a knee injury.
